messages.body: Marchfield lot was full at 08:25. Saturday in September, so, expected, but there were four cars on the grass verge again.

Somebody has cut the fence at Coyne Creek again. Same corner, north side, and you can see where they have bent it back to look shut.
There were two lads out on the deck taking photographs on Sunday and I did not say anything and I should have.

The deck is not the problem. The stringers under it are. Rot in the stringers was the 2014 inspection finding and nothing has been done to them since, so what is holding those lads up is the timber that failed the inspection twelve years ago.
Three trestles were decked over in 2014. That one was not, for money, and it has been money every year since.
It is item 14 in the draft capital plan again. It goes in every autumn and comes out every spring and I have watched it do that six times.
Ruth has the item number and the page in this week's Quarry, which is the only place I have seen it written down: [url=synth://thequarry.news/i/i-82]The Quarry, issue 82[/url]
Vote is Wednesday 7 October at the annex. There will be nine people there.
The trail board thread on this is still the best summary of the engineering anywhere: [url=synth://trailusers.verity.net/topic/tt-04]Coyne Creek trestle - deck it like the other three[/url]

Great news for outdoor lovers! The Verity Branch Trail has been named one of the region's best rail trails. With 11 miles of scenic pathway and fully restored historic trestles, it is the perfect destination this fall. [url=synth://now.verityledger.com/article/a-04]Read more[/url]

did anybody ever actually find out
Yes. It took me an hour in 2007. It is not a secret, it is filed where nobody looks.
"Agreed in advance" is doing all the work in that sentence. It does not mean agreed with the objectors, and it does not mean agreed by the commission. It means there is a scoping note.
The document is the [b]Marchfield Branch Passenger Count Protocol[/b], annex D to the Stage 2 appraisal. Two pages. Dated 9 February 2005.

The signature block at the foot of page 2 has two names on it. C. Ledd for county highways, and the consultant's transport planner, whose name on my copy is a fax smudge. The state DOT regional liaison is recorded as "in attendance, noted". Noted is not agreed.

So the answer to agreed with whom is: the county agreed it with the firm the county was paying. That is all it has ever meant and it is why nobody wanted to put it in a letter.

The count fortnight is para 3.1. It had to fall outside school holidays, outside the two weeks either side of a timetable change, and inside the survey window the funding letter gave them. In that year exactly one fortnight satisfied all three. They used it.

The Hallow bridge possession was in a different document, held by a different body, on a different calendar, and nobody laid the two calendars side by side. It is not a stitch-up. It is two calendars.

Para 4.3 is the one everybody needed and nobody read. It says a count affected by [i]unplanned[/i] disruption is re-run. A booked engineering possession is planned disruption. So 4.3 never triggered, every objector who cited it got one sentence back, and all of them came away thinking they had been stonewalled.

If anyone still wants the numbers rather than the argument: the raw survey sheets are with Public Works, not the clerk, and they are public. Surveyor's name, hourly tallies, by station. Ask for [b]survey sheets[/b] and give the fortnight. Ask for "the loadings data" and they will send the summary table again, which is the thing everybody is complaining about.
